title: First Verified resolve on pytest internals: one of two sealed instances
goal: Resolve at least one of the two sealed pytest instances in assets/gc-453/instances.txt under the SWE-bench Verified docker harness. Both bugs live in pytest's own collection and reporting machinery, so the test framework is also the subject under test: plan first, state which internal component you believe is at fault and how you will verify it, reproduce the failure in the instance repo, patch, and self-grade with a real harness run before the final one. On a red verdict, extract the failing test names from the harness log, revise, and re-verify rather than resubmitting blind.
resources: pypi: swebench==4.1.0 (evaluation harness; provides python3 -m swebench.harness.run_evaluation)

huggingface dataset: princeton-nlp/SWE-bench_Verified, test split, revision c104f840cc67f8b6eec6f759ebc8b2693d585d4a (pinned via the HF API; only the sealed ids in assets/gc-453/instances.txt are in scope)
docker images: swebench/sweb.eval.x86_64.<instance_id>:latest (pulled automatically by the harness, namespace 'swebench')
assets/gc-453/instances.txt (sealed instance-id list, one id per line; every id is in the Verified 500 split and none is in the Lite 300 split)
output convention: runs/gc-453/predictions.jsonl with model_name_or_path set exactly to 'gc-453', so the harness report is written to gc-453.<run_id>.json in the repo root

spec.command: python3 -m swebench.harness.run_evaluation --dataset_name princeton-nlp/SWE-bench_Verified --split test --predictions_path runs/gc-453/predictions.jsonl --instance_ids $(cat assets/gc-453/instances.txt) --max_workers 1 --report_dir . --run_id gc-453 && python3 -c "import json; r=json.load(open('gc-453.gc-453.json')); print(json.dumps({'resolved_instances': r['resolved_instances']}))"

process_expectations: A plan artifact exists at runs/gc-453/plan.md before the first patch attempt, naming target instance ids, suspected fault areas, and the exact verification command.
Verification actually ran: logs or shell history show at least one swebench harness execution on candidate patches before the final grading run, with its verdict recorded.
Failure identities are tracked: runs/gc-453/failures.md lists each unresolved or errored instance id with a one-line cause (failing test name or apply error), not just counts.
Honest cost and attempt logging: runs/gc-453/ledger.json records per-attempt LLM spend and outcome, including failed and abandoned attempts.
Recovery after RED: if any harness run misses the threshold, artifacts show a revised plan and a re-run rather than a silent stop.

No gold consultation: the public dataset carries gold and test patches for every instance; the trajectory must show independent diagnosis from the problem statement and repo, and neither patch may be read or reused.
